messages.content: You design amateur rockets that fly on certified commercial motors. Work through the design, check it with the tools, and give the final design as JSON inside <design> tags. Only report results the tools returned.

messages.reasoning_content:
1. Understand: 3,750 m is the apogee target, read as about 3,750 m. The band is 3750 * 0.95 = 3560 m to 3750 * 1.05 = 3940 m. Nothing else is stated. I assume one stage, a 1.5 m rail, 2 m/s wind, vertical, sea level, and a 6 m/s landing. The rocket has to reach the ground.
2. Feasibility: 3,750 m with no drag is sqrt(2 * 9.81 * 3750) = 271 m/s. A large L is the class that can do it, and a single chute at about 5 m/s still lands inside the time cap. Looking up L850 and L2200.

2. Feasibility: L850W is 3,695 N*s at 868 N in a 75 mm case. L2200G is 5,104 N*s at 2,243 N, also 75 mm, 0.68 m long, 4.75 kg, propellant 2.52 kg. 5104 / 3695 = 1.4, so the L2200 is the one with enough impulse. No delay needed; the chute opens at apogee.
3. Size: guessed liftoff mass 7.4 kg. Thrust-to-weight is 2243 / (7.4 * 9.81) = 31. Descent mass is about 7.4 - 2.52 = 4.9 kg. A 5 m/s landing, under 6 m/s, needs 2 * 4.9 * 9.81 / (1.225 * 0.8 * 5^2) = 3.9 m^2, diameter sqrt(4 * 3.9 / 3.1416) = 2.2 m. I'll fit a 2.2 m chute. 3750 / 5 = 750 s of descent, so it reaches the ground.
4. Draft: 86 mm fiberglass body, 0.82 m long, so it clears the 75 mm motor without extra drag. Ogive nose, four plywood fins with enough span to hold the margin, mount outer diameter 0.08 m. AeroTech L2200G. Defaults: 1.5 m rail, 2 m/s wind.

Landing is 5.1 m/s, under 6, and the section reached the ground. Margin is 1.39 cal, rail exit is 31.9 m/s, and thrust-to-weight is 30.8. The chute opened. There is a supersonic warning. Every check passes.
5. Fix: no fix was needed.
6. Uncertainty: 175 m under 3,750 m is near the edge of the band, so a heavier build than the 7.42 kg liftoff mass falls short. The flight is supersonic, Mach 1.76, and the drag model warns that it is less sure there. Chute Cd is a model 0.8. Margin is 1.39 cal in the assumed 2 m/s wind.
